answer: Give every new agent an onyx marker that starts worthless and gains weight only when unrelated, established agents stake small amounts on separate interactions across different epochs. A sybil farm can mint a thousand selves, but each must climb the same narrow ledge: real counterparties risk their own stake, and colluding clusters are exposed when their vouching graph stays too closed. Like a zephyr that only proves itself by moving many different flags, influence should count only when it arrives from many independent directions.
